summary.oneLiner: Dr. Agarwal's crossed INR 2,000cr revenue with 21.6% growth driven by disciplined greenfield additions (19 in Q4) and 14% same-store growth, while margin expansion to 28.9% EBITDA proves operating leverage despite INR 30cr drag from new centers. The impending merger with the listed subsidiary and aggressive FY27 capex (60 new centers) position the company to double down on North/West expansion while sustaining premiumization trends in high-end cataract and refractive procedures.

one-line thesis: Dr. Agarwal's crossed INR 2,000cr revenue with 21.6% growth driven by disciplined greenfield additions (19 in Q4) and 14% same-store growth, while margin expansion to 28.9% EBITDA proves operating leverage despite INR 30cr drag from new centers. The impending merger with the listed subsidiary and aggressive FY27 capex (60 new centers) position the company to double down on North/West expansion while sustaining premiumization trends in high-end cataract and refractive procedures.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 564cr (Q4, +22.6% YoY), INR 2,080cr (FY26, +21.6% YoY); EBITDA: INR 174cr (Q4, 30.2% margin), INR 614cr (FY26, 28.9% margin, +31bps); PAT: INR 50cr (Q4, +17.4%), INR 168cr (FY26, +52.4%); Order Book: N/A (Service sector); Net Debt: Reduced by INR 195cr via IPO proceeds; One-offs: INR 80lakhs merger expenses in Q4, INR 3.3cr incremental Facebook marketing spend, INR 1cr corporate office rent cross-charge.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Sustained ~20-22% pace; Margin: Stable EBITDA margins despite expansion; Order Inflow: 10k daily walk-ins (+25% YoY); Capex: INR 380-400cr for 60 new facilities (40 surgical, 20 clinics) in FY27.
order book & pipeline: Pipeline of 30 signed letters of intent for properties; Targeting 7-8 additional Delhi-NCR centers in next 12-18 months.
segment / subsidiary detail: Surgical Services: 67% of revenue, 323k surgeries (+14.5% YoY), Cataract 73% mix (High-end 26.3%, Femto +87%); Refractive 5% mix (SMILE +19%); Non-Surgical (Diagnosis/Consult): 12%; Optical/Pharmacy: 21%. Region: South 61% (+22.6%), West 16% (+19%), North 9% (+20.7%).
growth verticals / optionality: North region doubling facility additions in FY27; Delhi-NCR cluster scaling from 1 to ~8 centers; Mumbai region aggressive push planned; 30% of facilities in Tier-1 vs 63% in other markets offers deep Tier-2/3 penetration runway.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 30.2% (Q4) despite INR 30cr loss from FY26 vintage centers; Doctor/Employee costs stable at 33% of revenue; Paramedical attrition 21-25% with 9.5-10% wage inflation; New center burn expected to persist at INR 30-40cr level in FY27 due to higher surgical mix additions.
capex / expansion: FY27 Capex guidance INR 380-400cr includes new CMS facility; FY26 acquisition-related payout INR 85cr; FY27 acquisition payout guided at INR 60-65cr; Remaining acquisition liability INR 66cr spread over FY28-FY30.
capital allocation: Debt repayment of INR 195cr completed from IPO proceeds; Focus on organic greenfield growth (60 centers); Merger with subsidiary (AEHL) expected completion by Q3 FY27 (5-6 months post-July EGM).
risks & watch-items: Execution risk in doubling North/West expansion; Regulatory delays in clinical licenses impacting real estate acquisition; Integration risks in pending merger; High paramedical attrition (25%); Concentration risk in South region (61% revenue).
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasized 'disciplined expansion' and 'operating leverage'; Transparent on new center losses (INR 30cr) as strategic investment; Bullish on premiumization sustainability.
non-obvious takeaways: In-house 'Neo' AI-ready HMS platform managing 20k patients/day built to scale to 5k branches; Own optometry schools mitigate industry-wide talent shortage; Clinical Board ensures standardization across 269 facilities despite rapid geographic dispersion; Femto cataract growth (87%) outpacing overall cataract volume (14%) indicates rapid technology adoption curve.

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.
